frequency_question: How often do executive branch nominations submitted to the U.S. Senate succeed in achieving a confirmed floor vote within a 70-day window?
membership_rule: Includes all Cabinet-level and major statutory agency (like FDA, CDC, EPA) nominations that reached the Senate floor or were actively processed within 70 days of initial submission; excludes recess appointments or withdrawn nominations where intent to pursue was abandoned.
provenance_note: 5 cases named, 6 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 5 named; believed roughly 6 in total for this specific tier of agency/department head in compressed windows.
known_gaps: Excludes lower-tier sub-cabinet confirmations which face different procedural volumes.
skeleton: Recent fast-tracked health agency and department head confirmations over the last three administrations (Obama, Trump, Biden), examining the subset processed within compressed timeframes under unified or divided Senate control.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 6 total comparable high-profile health nominations processed in a timely manner.
validity_reason: Base rate tied to Senate filibuster rules for executive nominees (simple majority rule established in 2013), which remains stable through the current congressional term.
